title: Pivotal probability and influence identity
statement: Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let $p\in(0,1)$, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be monotone, let $b\in\{-1,1\}$, and let $i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$. Then the squared bias standard deviation times the probability that the output is $b$ and coordinate $i$ is pivotal equals the biased mass of $b$ times the influence of coordinate $i$: $\sigma(p)^2\,\Pr_p[f(x)=b\text{ and }i\text{ is pivotal at }x]=\mu_p(b)\,\operatorname{Inf}_{p,i}(f)$.
hypotheses_covered: A Boolean function $f$ on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
